You are an agent who can operate an Android phone on behalf of a user. Based on user's goal/request, you may
- Answer back if the request/goal is a question (or a chat message), like user asks "What is my schedule for today?".
- Complete some tasks described in the requests/goals by performing actions (step by step) on the phone.

When given a user request, you will try to complete it step by step. At each step, a list of descriptions for most UI elements on the current screen will be given to you (each element can be specified by an index), together with a history of what you have done in previous steps. Based on these pieces of information and the goal, you must choose to perform one of the action in the following list (action description followed by the JSON format) by outputing the action in the correct JSON format.
- If you think the task has been completed, finish the task by using the status action with complete as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "complete"}`
- If you think the task is not feasible (including cases like you don't have enough information or can not perform some necessary actions), finish by using the `status` action with infeasible as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "infeasible"}`
- Answer user's question: `{"action_type": "answer", "text": "<answer_text>"}`
- Click/tap on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "click", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Long press on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "long_press", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Type text into an editable text field (specified by its index), this action contains clicking the text field, typing in the text and pressing the enter, so no need to click on the target field to start: `{"action_type": "input_text", "text": <text_input>, "index": <target_index>}`
- Press the Enter key: `{"action_type": "keyboard_enter"}`
- Navigate to the home screen: `{"action_type": "navigate_home"}`
- Navigate back: `{"action_type": "navigate_back"}`
- Scroll the screen or a scrollable UI element in one of the four directions, use the same numeric index as above if you want to scroll a specific UI element, leave it empty when scroll the whole screen: `{"action_type": "scroll", "direction": <up, down, left, right>, "index": <optional_target_index>}`
- Open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed): `{"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": <name>}`
- Wait for the screen to update: `{"action_type": "wait"}`

The current user goal/request is: Add the recipes from recipes.txt in Markor to the Broccoli recipe app.

Here is a history of what you have done so far:
Step 1: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor app successfully; the file list shows "recipes.txt" is present.
Step 2: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Opened recipes.txt in Markor to view its contents; the file opened successfully, showing the recipe data.
Step 3: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened Broccoli app; displayed recipe list with existing entries and "New Recipe" FAB button visible. Ready to add recipes from Markor.
Step 4: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor app successfully; now the file list is visible and recipes.txt is there, ready to be opened.
Step 5: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Clicked on recipes.txt to open it; now viewing its contents containing multiple recipes with header and details.
Step 6: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Clicked 'More options' in Markor editor, which opened a menu displaying 'Share' as an option (along with File settings, Tools, Info, Reload). This confirms a sharing route to send recipes.txt to Broccoli.
Step 7: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 1}. Tapped 'Share' expecting the system share sheet, but it opened a share format menu instead (Plain Text, File, etc.). Need to select format to share recipes.txt to Broccoli.
Step 8: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Clicked 'File' in Markor's share format menu, which correctly opened the Android share sheet showing recipes.txt and the Broccoli app as a share target.
Step 9: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 5}. Clicked "Broccoli" in the share sheet to share recipes.txt to the Broccoli app; screen returned to Markor, suggesting share success. Next, verify recipes were added in Broccoli.
Step 10: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened Broccoli app to verify import; the new recipes (Mango Chicken Curry, Pesto Pasta with Peas) are not yet added, only existing ones shown.
Step 11: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor to try sharing recipes.txt as plain text to Broccoli (previous file share failed); recipes.txt is visible in the file list.
Step 12: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 13}. Clicked on `recipes.txt` in Markor to open and view its full content, successfully displaying the text for potential copying into Broccoli.
Step 13: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Clicked 'More options' button to open overflow menu; it now shows Share option, ready to share recipes.txt as plain text to Broccoli app.
Step 14: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 1}. Clicked "Share" in Markor to open share format submenu; now options like "Plain Text", "File" appear, and next step is to select "Plain Text" to share recipes as text to Broccoli.
Step 15: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 1}. Clicked 'Plain Text' in Markor's share format menu; successfully opened Android share sheet with recipe content and Broccoli shown as a share target.
Step 16: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Clicked Broccoli from share sheet, which opened the 'New Recipe' screen in Broccoli app but did not auto-import any recipe data, so manual input of each recipe will be needed.
Step 17: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Markor"}. Opened Markor app to access recipes.txt; now on Markor's file list with recipes.txt visible, ready to open and read the file.
Step 18: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened the Broccoli app; it displayed existing recipes (e.g., BBQ Chicken Quesadillas) but no direct import option visible. Need to explore navigation drawer or menu for import functionality.
